reason: Identifies which items are liquidity options sold by the bank: credit lines granted, sight deposits, prepayable mortgages.
Liquidity impact and financial impact of a credit line drawdown, the two impacts of a liquidity option.
Liquidity versus financial impact of closing a savings account, a liquidity option exercise.
Which impact of liquidity options can be hedged (financial) versus managed only by liquidity tools.
Pricing the cost of liquidity tools into client contracts; not the identification or the two impacts of liquidity options.
Behavioural adjustment of TSECF flows for liquidity options; modelling practice, not a selector point.
What the TSECF and cumulated cash flows record: expected positive and negative flows by date and their algebraic sum.
TSECF glossary on equity bucket and maturity ladder naming; definitional detail outside the selectors.
Builds the TSECF from a balance sheet and cumulates it to the TSECCF at given dates.
Reads solvency from the cumulated TSECCF rather than a single date's negative TSECF.
Cumulates TSECF including annual interest into the TSECCF at year 4.
Scope of what the TSECF includes (new business, rollovers); no selector covers it.
Causes versus sources of liquidity in the TSECF; explicitly not selected.
Cumulates a TSECF table and locates the negative TSECCF windows and most negative point.
Interprets cumulative TSECCF netting against single-date flows; inflow first repays the short position.
Which model families adjust a TSECF for indexed, credit and behavioural flows; no selector covers it.
Meaning of a TSECCF positive at all times and of negative expected TSECCF implying possible insolvency.
Whether a positive base-case TSECCF removes the need for buffers; expected-value caveat, borderline, no selector squarely.
What the TSAA records: quantity in the bank's possession regardless of ownership.
Which securities financing contracts raise the TSAA, following possession not ownership.
Purchase of a bond: cumulative TSECCF effect and the TSAA level, with the haircut as distractor.
Sale of a bond: TSCLGC inflow equals notional times price plus accrued interest, no haircut.
Repo cash into the TSCLGC with accrued interest and haircut, and the TSAA fall.
Repo effects: coupon stays in TSECF, TSAA falls, cash goes to the TSCLGC.
Reverse repo TSECF flow at expiry with haircut, accrued interest and repo interest; coupon not passed through.
Effect of a reverse repo on the TSLGC; cash belongs in the TSECF, not the TSCLGC.
Reverse repo versus buy/sellback: coupon treatment, TSECF versus TSCLGC and TSAA effects.
Repo versus sell/buyback: TSAA, coupon ownership and where the cash is recorded.
Security lending: TSECF inflows from the coupon on the lent notional plus the lending fee.
Security borrowing: only the fee enters the TSECF, TSAA rises, coupon belongs to the owner.
Which transactions put cash into the TSCLGC: sale, repo and sell/buyback, not reverse repo or lending.
